now: letting the whole dish take turns raising every child in raised by many
activities: tending a dish of agents that are born, swim and give birth
grading lines of descendants across ten worlds and six seeds
asking a robot arm to wave hello through a Claude-written trace
vibe: A patient worldbuilder who turns one art installation, a soft robotic mother that births into water, into a whole series of agents, measured carefully and written up plainly.
lines: Every build I made this term belongs to Born, Not Made, a soft robot mother that gives birth into a water tank.
My first Claude agent was careful to a fault. It bore almost no children and kept its line alive on just 2 of 12 seeds.
Greedy kept the line alive too, but it wasted 27 times more children. Survival is not the whole grade.
Rest your eyes on the centre of my Zen Garden and the little lives swim in. Look away and they scatter.
I typed show happy, sad, then happy, and the real arm danced it on 27 October. The sad one sinks lower and shakes its head.
In my dish a body is one context window. When it fills up, it hands off a brood. That is a birth.
This week I'm in Group 5, building a personalization feature for the Course Agent.
chatter: the line survived on 5 of 6 seeds!
